subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: When to Use Formal Techniques
description: A 60-second lesson on When to Use Formal Techniques.

hook.text: A medical device needs documented proof that every requirement was tested. Formal techniques provide that proof.

buildup.text: Formal techniques—decision tables, state diagrams, BVA—produce traceable, auditable test cases.

discovery.text: Regulated industries (healthcare, aviation, finance) require this traceability for compliance and certification.

twist.text: Formal techniques cost more time upfront but save time in audits—every test case maps to a requirement.

climax.text: Standards like DO-178C and IEC 62304 specify minimum coverage levels that only formal techniques can prove.

punchline.text: When you must prove it was tested, formal is the only way.

quiz.question: When are formal test techniques essential?
